title: Observational Astronomy
tagline: Learn the night sky with your eyes, binoculars, and eventually a telescope.
curricula: University Astronomy 101 syllabi and the Astronomical League's observing programs
endpoint: from nothing to reading the northern night sky unaided
about: Observational astronomy is the practice of reading the night sky with your own eyes — finding your bearings among the constellations, following the Moon and planets through their cycles, and learning to see faint things well. This category walks from a first night under the sky through naked-eye navigation, binocular astronomy, and deep-sky observing, to choosing and using a telescope. No equipment is needed for most of the path: the sky is free, and the skill is in the looking.
